ARBA00022603

View original ARBA rule on UniProt

Type: ARBA
Status: COMPLETE
Action: ACCEPT
Confidence: 0.70
Rule as retrieved: 2026-11-12
Condition sets examined: 624 of 624

Description

Assigns the UniProt keyword Methyltransferase (KW-0489) from 624 alternative condition sets of InterPro, FunFam, PANTHER and taxon conditions.

The domain overlap table is not shown for this review. It is drawn from a cached analysis of the rule's condition sets, and the cache does not match the sets recorded here.

Review Summary

Accuracy: the rule assigns the keyword Methyltransferase (KW-0489) from 624 alternative condition sets. On 2026-11-12 each of the 624 sets of the rule as fetched on 2026-11-10 was turned into a UniProtKB query and counted against Swiss-Prot. Every set has reviewed matches (2 to 844 per set, median 8; 29761 summed over sets) and no set has a reviewed match that lacks the keyword. TrEMBL matches were not inspected, and the individual sets are not recorded in this review. Meaning and parsimony: the keyword names an enzyme class and the sets select methyltransferase families, one or a few sets each. A systematic sample of 12 sets (every 52nd) gave twelve different families: rRNA methyltransferases RsmH, RlmC and RsmA, catechol O-methyltransferases, the tetrahydromethanopterin S-methyltransferase subunit A, fungal polyketide synthases keyworded as methyltransferases, fungal secondary-metabolite methyltransferases, betaine-homocysteine S-methyltransferase, SETDB histone methyltransferases, NSUN2, PRMT9 and the citrate synthase lysine methyltransferase. The keyword is the level at which the class is defined, so a rule spanning many families is what a keyword rule is for. Redundancy between sets was not measured.

Action Rationale

No set assigns the keyword to a reviewed protein that lacks it, and the sets sampled select what the label names. Confidence is moderate because the check used reviewed entries only, meaning was judged from 12 of 624 sets, and overlap between sets was not measured.

Biological Meaning

COHERENT

Systematic sample of 12 of 624 sets, positions 1, 53, 105 and so on in the served rule, each identified from the names of its reviewed matches. Every sampled set selects one methyltransferase family or, in one case, multidomain polyketide synthases that Swiss-Prot keywords as methyltransferases. The review records no condition sets, so units are named by their signatures and not by set number. This is a keyword rule, so rule_redundancy.tsv has no row for it.

The consequent term has descendant terms. 0 condition set(s) are also matched by a rule asserting a more specific term. 12 condition set(s) were examined for this judgement.

Assessments

ACCEPTABLE

624 sets, none without reviewed matches and none with a reviewed match lacking the keyword. The median set has 8 reviewed matches, so many sets are narrow family or subfamily signatures. Whether sets of this rule are contained in one another was not measured. No single signature could stand in for a class that spans several unrelated folds. keyword_redundancy.tsv: none of the 624 condition sets is matched by a rule for a descendant keyword.

APPROPRIATE

159 of the 624 sets carry a taxon condition. In the five sampled sets that have one, all reviewed matches within the taxon carry the keyword. Whether each restriction is as wide as the family was not examined; a narrow one limits coverage only.

review_summary: >-
  Accuracy: the rule assigns the keyword Methyltransferase (KW-0489) from 624 alternative condition sets.
  On 2026-11-12 each of the 624 sets of the rule as fetched on 2026-11-10 was turned into a UniProtKB
  query and counted against Swiss-Prot. Every set has reviewed matches (2 to 844 per set, median 8; 29761
  summed over sets) and no set has a reviewed match that lacks the keyword. TrEMBL matches were not inspected,
  and the individual sets are not recorded in this review. Meaning and parsimony: the keyword names an
  enzyme class and the sets select methyltransferase families, one or a few sets each. A systematic sample
  of 12 sets (every 52nd) gave twelve different families: rRNA methyltransferases RsmH, RlmC and RsmA,
  catechol O-methyltransferases, the tetrahydromethanopterin S-methyltransferase subunit A, fungal polyketide
  synthases keyworded as methyltransferases, fungal secondary-metabolite methyltransferases, betaine-homocysteine
  S-methyltransferase, SETDB histone methyltransferases, NSUN2, PRMT9 and the citrate synthase lysine
  methyltransferase. The keyword is the level at which the class is defined, so a rule spanning many families
  is what a keyword rule is for. Redundancy between sets was not measured.
action: ACCEPT
action_rationale: >-
  No set assigns the keyword to a reviewed protein that lacks it, and the sets sampled select what the
  label names. Confidence is moderate because the check used reviewed entries only, meaning was judged
  from 12 of 624 sets, and overlap between sets was not measured.
confidence: 0.7
